  "agent": "The DCI",

  "situation": "In 1973, the DCI had to choose an arrangement for producing National Intelligence Estimates. The existing structure centered on the Office of National Estimates. Intelligence community analysts drafted estimates; they often came from CIA, but some came from other agencies and departments. Agencies had previously been asked to coordinate drafts only after they were written. An alternative structure could use National Intelligence Officers with expertise in specific fields, supported by analysts seconded from across the intelligence community. Under that structure, agencies could take part in drafting from the beginning, while officers managed community relations, supervised estimate production, and addressed intelligence consumers' needs in their areas.",
  "question": "What should the DCI do about the structure for producing National Intelligence Estimates and the timing of other agencies' participation?",
